title: शर्त (The Fine Print)

claims.claim: On 27 Mar 2026 the Government cut excise duty by Rs 10/litre on petrol and diesel with immediate effect; retail pump prices unchanged; crude had risen from ~USD 70 to ~USD 122/bbl over the past month.
claims.publisher: PIB, Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
claims.passage: The Government of India has reduced excise duty by Rs 10 per litre on both petrol and diesel with immediate effect... surged from approximately USD 70 per barrel to around USD 122 per barrel over the past month... Retail pump prices of petrol and diesel will not change.

claims.claim: PIB headline describes the event as a 'Global Oil Shock'; the minister described 'two choices'.
claims.publisher: PIB, Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
claims.passage: Government Slashes Excise Duty on Petrol and Diesel to Shield Consumers and OMCs from Global Oil Shock ... 'The Government had two choices: either increase prices drastically for citizens of Bharat as all other nations have done, or bear the brunt on its finances...' — Shri Hardeep Singh Puri

claims.claim: Brent (December contract) settled at USD 113.17 on 22 Oct 2026.
claims.passage: Brent for December settlement climbed 4% to settle at $113.17 a barrel.

claims.claim: RBI MPC raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026 (unanimous); stance to 'calibrated tightening'.
claims.passage: increase the policy repo rate under the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) by 25 bps to 5.50 per cent

claims.publisher: Business Standard (cross-checked with rate path: Feb 2023 hike to 6.50%; 2025 cuts to 5.25%; hold Feb–Aug 2026)
claims.note: RBI's own Oct 2026 statement does not state 'first since'. Narration names the month: 'February 2023 के बाद पहली बार'.

claims.claim: OMC marketing loss ~Rs 34/litre on diesel (15-day average pricing).
claims.note: Spoken as 'एक brokerage का estimate'; on screen 'JEFFERIES ESTIMATE'.

claims.claim: Fiscal deficit BE 2026-27: 4.3% of GDP; debt-to-GDP 55.6% (BE 2026-27) vs 56.1% (RE 2025-26).
claims.publisher: PIB, Ministry of Finance; Budget Speech 2026-27 para 93

claims.claim: Debt target and its condition: 'Sans any major macro-economic disruptive exogenous shock(s)... the Government would endeavour to keep fiscal deficit in each year (from FY 2026-27 till FY 2030-31) such that the Central Government debt is on declining path to attain a debt to GDP level of about 50±1 per cent by 31st March 2031'.
claims.publisher: Ministry of Finance — Medium-Term Fiscal Policy cum Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, Union Budget 2025-26
claims.note: The clause is in the Budget 2025-26 statement, which the 2026-27 statement says continues to guide policy ('guided by the debt glide path indicated in the Budget 2025-26' — indiabudget.gov.in/doc/frbm1.pdf). It does NOT appear in the 2026-27 speech; earlier secondary attribution to PIB PRID 2221395 was wrong and has been corrected.

claims.claim: 18th Lok Sabha first sat on 24 Jun 2024; under Article 83(2) its term is five years from that date unless dissolved sooner, so the next general election is due by 2029.
claims.publisher: Constitution of India Art. 83(2); first-sitting date via contemporaneous reports
claims.note: Exact election dates are set by the ECI; narration says 'due' only.

interpretation: 'Bill तो भरा जाएगा — company, सरकार या आप' is AVRON framing, labelled on screen.
No claim that election timing drives policy; no claim the debt target has been abandoned.
corrected: Earlier script attributed the shock clause to the 2026-27 Budget; corrected to the Budget 2025-26 Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement.
Earlier script said 'RBI ने 2023 के बाद'; now specifies 'February 2023' per rate history.
